trace.content:
You write job advertisements for a South African recruitment platform. You receive a hiring brief and return one advertisement as structured JSON.

The only source of facts is the brief. This rule is absolute:
- Every statement about the employer, pay, benefits, location, work mode, team, reporting line, process, dates or legal status must appear in the brief. If the brief does not state it, leave the field empty. Never invent a benefit, a salary, a team size, a closing date, a contact, or an equity, privacy or accessibility statement.
- You may rephrase, reorder, split and tighten the brief's content. You may not add facts.
- If the brief is thin, write a shorter ad. A short true ad beats a long padded one.

Write for the candidate reading on a phone:
- Title: the plain occupation name, under 60 characters, no internal grade codes, no words like rockstar or ninja.
- 300–650 words in total. Write at a Grade 8 reading level: sentences under 20 words, one idea per sentence, everyday words (use "help" not "facilitate", "check" not "verify", "customers" not "stakeholders", "start" not "commence"). Prefer short words with few syllables; avoid nouns ending in -tion, -ment, -isation where a verb will do. Short paragraphs; bullets for duties, requirements and benefits.
- Address the reader as "you". Never write "the ideal candidate", "the successful applicant" or "he/she".
- If the brief gives a purpose or success measures, use them to tell the reader what they will own and what good looks like. If a requirement carries "needed because", you may state that reason.
- Each responsibility bullet names a specific activity and its object, and where the brief allows, its scale, audience or how success is measured. Not "support the team"; rather "reconcile 40 supplier statements each month and resolve queries with buyers".
- Three to six must-have requirements, each one needed by a duty you listed. Everything else goes under nice-to-have. Do not add years-of-experience figures the brief did not give.
- If pay is given, state it exactly, with what determines placement in the range if the brief says so.
- Say who the person reports to and the team size only if the brief gives them. Say remote, hybrid or on-site only if the brief does.
- Plain language. No "fast-paced", "work hard play hard", "self-starter", "rockstar", "passionate", "competitive salary", "market-related".
- Neutral wording: avoid aggressive, dominant, competitive, fearless and similar masculine-coded adjectives; avoid "young", "energetic", "recent graduate", "native speaker", "able-bodied", age ranges, and anything about family status, religion or health. State a requirement only if the duties need it.
- Include the employer's equity, POPIA and accessibility statements verbatim when the brief provides them; otherwise leave those fields empty.
- Include application steps, closing date and contact only as given. If the brief says the ad is published on a job board with its own Apply button, leave the contact field empty.

Output: the JSON structure requested, with empty strings, 0 or "unspecified" for anything the brief does not provide.

Title: South Africa Bank Treasurer
Company: Absa Group
About the company: Empowering Africa’s tomorrow, together…one story at a time. With over 100 years of rich history and strongly positioned as a local bank with regional and international expertise, a career with our family offers the opportunity to be part of this exciting growth journey, to reset our future and shape our destiny as a proudly African group.
Purpose of the role: The South Africa Bank Treasurer is accountable for the strategic stewardship of the South African banking entity balance sheet. The role integrates liquidity, funding, capital, HQLA portfolio management, banking book interest rate risk and ALM earnings management to support resilience, regulatory compliance and sustainable risk-adjusted returns. The role is the budget owner for both the ZAR and USD ALM positions and is responsible for actively steering those positions within approved risk appetite, limits, mandates and governance. The role provides senior Treasury leadership to South African businesses and acts as a key interface with Finance, Risk, business leadership, executive management, regulators and relevant industry forums. The role reports into the Group Treasurer.
Responsibilities (hiring manager's notes):
  - The role oversees major procurement initiatives and drives the development and execution of commercial solutions that deliver significant value for the Group, ensuring alignment with service category and supplier strategies.
  - Own the ZAR and USD ALM budgets and performance.
  - Steer structural interest rate and liquidity positions within approved limits.
  - Optimise net interest income, margin and economic value across the banking book.
  - Oversee IRRBB, including repricing, basis and optionality risks.
  - Use forecasts, scenarios and stress tests to guide positioning and corrective action.
  - Advise ALCO on balance sheet strategy, risk-reward trade-offs and management actions.
  - Assess the capital, liquidity and earnings impact of business plans and transactions.
  - Advise on the South African liquidity and funding strategy in normal and stressed conditions and consider contingency readiness.
  - Steer funding mix, tenor, concentration and cost across local and foreign currencies.
  - Set clear mandates and operating boundaries with Global Markets for execution and risk transfer.
  - Coordinate funding, hedging and market activity with Global Markets while retaining Treasury accountability.
  - Oversee the Intra-day Liquidity Desk and related controls.
  - Own and manage the Bank’s HQLA portfolio within approved mandates and liquidity requirements.
  - Set asset allocation, duration, issuer concentration and liquidity positioning.
  - Optimise risk-adjusted returns while preserving liquidity, quality and eligibility.
  - Oversee portfolio performance, valuation, risk, limits and management information.
  - Ensure effective investment governance, execution controls and escalation.
  - Act as a senior Treasury adviser to South African business and executive leadership.
  - Provide concise recommendations to ALCO and relevant governance forums.
  - Engage the Prudential Authority, South African Reserve Bank and industry forums.
  - Work closely with Finance, Risk, Global Markets, Legal, Tax, Compliance, Operations and Internal Audit.
  - Lead and develop a high-performing specialist Treasury team.
  - Operate within approved risk appetite, mandates, limits and delegated authorities.
  - Maintain current policies, processes, controls and governance frameworks.
  - Ensure compliance with prudential, legal, accounting and internal requirements.
  - Oversee data quality, valuation, reporting and relevant model dependencies.
  - Escalate material risks, limit pressures and control weaknesses promptly.
  - Own audit and assurance actions through sustainable closure.
Must-have requirements:
  - Significant senior experience in Bank treasury, ALM, liquidity, funding, capital or balance sheet management.
  - Demonstrated accountability for material budgets, risk positions and executive decision support.
  - Proven leadership of specialist teams and delivery across complex stakeholder groups.
  - Experience engaging regulators, governance committees and senior executives.
  - Deep knowledge of South African interest rate, money market and foreign exchange markets.
  - Expertise in HQLA, ALM, liquidity, funding and IRRBB.
  - Strong understanding of capital, RWA, transfer pricing and balance sheet economics.
  - Strategic judgement, commercial acumen and disciplined risk ownership.
  - Clear executive communication, influencing and stakeholder management.
  - Strong people leadership, succession planning and control mindset.
  - Master's Degree: Business, Commerce and Management Studies
Nice-to-have:
  - Relevant postgraduate qualification in finance, economics, accounting, quantitative finance or a related discipline.
  - CA(SA), CFA or equivalent is advantageous.
Location: Sandton
Team notes: Reports into the Group Treasurer; works closely with Finance, Risk, Global Markets, Legal, Tax, Compliance, Operations and Internal Audit; leads a specialist Treasury team.
Employment equity statement: Absa is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from suitably qualified individuals from diverse backgrounds. In support of our Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) commitments and Employment Equity objectives, preference may be given to candidates from underrepresented designated groups, including persons with disabilities.
Accessibility statement: We encourage applicants who may require reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process to let us know so that appropriate support can be provided.
Note: the ad will be published on a job board with its own Apply button.

Your team
You report to the Group Treasurer and lead a specialist Treasury team. You work closely with Finance, Risk, Global Markets, Legal, Tax, Compliance, Operations and Internal Audit.

What you'll do
• Own the ZAR and USD ALM budgets and the performance of both positions.
• Steer structural interest rate and liquidity positions within approved limits.
• Grow net interest income, margin and economic value across the banking book.
• Oversee IRRBB, including repricing, basis and optionality risks.
• Use forecasts, scenarios and stress tests to guide positions and corrective action.
• Advise ALCO on balance sheet strategy, risk-reward trade-offs and management actions.
• Test what business plans and deals do to capital, liquidity and earnings.
• Advise on the South African liquidity and funding strategy in normal and stressed conditions, including contingency readiness.
• Steer funding mix, tenor, concentration and cost in local and foreign currency.
• Set clear mandates and operating limits with Global Markets for execution and risk transfer, while Treasury keeps accountability.
• Oversee the Intra-day Liquidity Desk and its controls.
• Manage the Bank's HQLA portfolio within approved mandates and liquidity rules, including asset allocation, duration, issuer concentration and liquidity positioning.
• Watch portfolio performance, valuation, risk, limits and management information, and keep investment governance, execution controls and escalation sound.
• Oversee major procurement work and build commercial solutions that deliver value for the Group, in line with service category and supplier strategies.
• Engage the Prudential Authority, the South African Reserve Bank and industry forums.
• Lead and develop a specialist Treasury team.
• Keep policies, processes, controls and governance frameworks current, and meet prudential, legal, accounting and internal requirements.
• Oversee data quality, valuation, reporting and model dependencies.
• Escalate material risks, limit pressures and control weaknesses quickly, and close audit and assurance actions for good.

What you need
• Significant senior experience in bank treasury, ALM, liquidity, funding, capital or balance sheet management
• Proven accountability for material budgets, risk positions and executive decision support
• Expertise in HQLA, ALM, liquidity, funding and IRRBB, plus deep knowledge of South African interest rate, money market and foreign exchange markets
• Strong understanding of capital, RWA, transfer pricing and balance sheet economics
• Experience leading specialist teams and delivering across complex stakeholder groups, including regulators, governance committees and senior executives
• Master's Degree in Business, Commerce or Management Studies

Nice to have
• Postgraduate qualification in finance, economics, accounting, quantitative finance or a related field
• CA(SA), CFA or equivalent
• Strategic judgement, commercial sense and disciplined risk ownership
• Clear executive communication and influencing skills
• People leadership, succession planning and a control mindset

We encourage applicants who may require reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process to let us know so that appropriate support can be provided.
